preamble: Weakening of the palatal nasal stop [ɲ] to a palatal glide removes the oral closure while keeping the palatal place. In Daco-Romanian the [ɲ] that arose from Latin /nj/ was denasalized to [j] (calcaneum > călcâi 'heel'), while Aromanian and the Banat dialect keep [ɲ]. In most Common Turkic languages Proto-Turkic *ń, still written as a nasal in Old Turkic, became y (*kōń 'sheep' > Kazakh qoy). In Brazilian and Angolan Portuguese, written nh is realized as a nasalized glide [j̃].

examples.note: The Banat dialect keeps the nasal in călcâni.

examples.to: Kazakh, Kyrgyz qoy / koy; Uzbek qoʻy; Turkish koyun
examples.note: Old Turkic and Karakhanid koń / kōńug keep the palatal nasal.

examples.to: Kazakh küyüw, Uyghur köymek, Turkmen köýmek (verbal nouns / infinitives)
examples.note: The same *ń > y outcome appears across the Kipchak, Karluk and Oghuz branches.
In Brazil and Angola nh is realized as a nasal palatal approximant [j̃], which nasalizes the preceding vowel.

Proto-Timbíra changed onset *ñ to *j; Tapayúna changed coda *ñ to j. Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: ñ = [ɲ], j = [j ~ ʒ], c = [tʃ ~ tɕ ~ ts ~ c], ĵ = [dʒ ~ ɟ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ê/ô = close-mid [e]/[o], ṭʰ = aspirated alveolar stop, mb/nd = post-oralized nasals; a final ’ marks a coda without echo vowel, X // Y gives phrase-medial // prepausal allomorphs.

Proto-Akuwẽ reflects coda *ñ as j phrase-medially and as zero before a pause. Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: ñ = [ɲ], j = [j ~ ʒ], c = [tʃ ~ tɕ ~ ts ~ c], ĵ = [dʒ ~ ɟ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ê/ô = close-mid [e]/[o], ṭʰ = aspirated alveolar stop, mb/nd = post-oralized nasals; a final ’ marks a coda without echo vowel, X // Y gives phrase-medial // prepausal allomorphs.
Proto-Gbaya and daughter forms from Moñino's comparative lexicon as tabulated on Wikipedia; y = [j]. Gbaya Bodoe, Gbeya ɲín and Mbodomo ɲíní keep the palatal nasal.
Gbaya Bodoe, Gbeya, Mbodomo and Bofi keep ɲɔŋ.
